newsitem.title: UK: Virgin CableTel launch internet venture.
newsitem.headline: Virgin CableTel launch internet venture.

text.p: British entrepreneur Richard Branson and International CableTel of the United States on Tuesday launched Virgin Net, a new internet service provider.

Virgin Net is a joint venture between Virgin Communications, part of British entrepreneur Richard Branson's Virgin Group, and CableTel unit Cable Online. The joint venture was originally announced in May.
Virgin Communications has 51 percent of Virgin Net, with CableTel owning the remaining 49 percent.
Branson told a news conference Virgin Net was the first "consumer-friendly" internet service provider. It is due officially to come on-line on November 28, with subscription set at 10 stg a month.
Virgin Net hopes to have about 20,000 subscribers by the end of the year.
The service will offer subscribers access to a directory of 3,000 web pages selected by Virgin to make searches quicker, as well as providing access to the World Wide Web.
"Virgin Net is about people accessing information and entertainment," Branson said.
"We have also dispensed with the tricky graphics that eat up memory and slow down searches," he added.

CableTel's managing director, John Gregg, said the new service is targeted on the British market. "Virgin's role is to provide marketing prowess, while CableTel will provide the national cable network," he said.
But asked if Virgin was looking to expand the service abroad, Branson said: "I think it's very unlikely we won't very soon."
Asked how much Virgin invested in the project, Branson said: "You're probably looking at 50 to 100 million stg between Virgin and CableTel after we've been in the business for four to five years."
"We estimate that Virgin Net will be able to stand alone as a profitable business within a couple of years time," he added.
Virgin Net will use broadband technology, which allows information such as pictures to be sent along a phone cable far quicker than conventional narrowband lines.
"CableTel has invested one billion stg over the past three years laying down our broadband terrestial broadcast Network," Gregg said.

Asked if his airline Virgin Atlantic Airways would provide its passengers with access to the new internet service, Branson said he hoped to provide live television on his aircraft "within the next 12 months" with in-flight internet access to follow.
